messages:
acme-platform-admin: Hi team — after our recent Okta groups sync, our security engineers can no longer view audit logs in the Redwood Console. They get a 403. We rely on those logs for compliance. Can you help?
Maria Chen: Sorry about that — can you confirm the org id and which user tried to view the logs? Also, is this SSO-only for the org or do you have local accounts? :eyes:
acme-platform-admin: Org ID: org_0a1b2c3d. User: emma@acme.co. SSO-only. We rolled a group mapping change ~2h before this started.
Maria Chen: Thanks — can you try to open Console > Observability > Audit logs and paste any error text or a screenshot? Also, any request id you see?
acme-platform-admin: Screenshot attached in thread (not included here). Error in browser devtools: 
```
GET /api/v1/audit/logs 403 {"error":"forbidden","message":"missing entitlement: audit_logs:read"}
```
Maria Chen: That error message helps — indicates the token didn't have entitlement `audit_logs:read`. I'm going to reproduce with an account I control. @Ajay can you look at the authz logs for org_0a1b2c3d around 2026-02-03T14:00Z?
Ajay Patel: Pulling logs. One sec.
Ajay Patel: I can see a 403 for subject=emma@acme.co, reason="missing_entitlement", attributes: `groups=[devs,security-readonly]`, token_scopes=[openid,profile,email]. No `audit_logs:read` entitlement returned by the entitlement service.
Maria Chen: Thanks — can you check the SAML assertion we received from Okta for that user? @idp-bot if you can paste the last SAML attributes for emma@acme.co?
idp-bot: SAML assertion (excerpt):
```
<Attribute Name="groups">devs,security-readonly</Attribute>
<Attribute Name="roles">engineer</Attribute>
<Attribute Name="entitlements" />
```
Kate Reynolds: Looks like Okta isn't sending our expected `entitlements` attribute. We map `entitlements` -> Redwood entitlements during SAML processing. If it's empty, users won't get `audit_logs:read` or retention entitlements.
Rob Silva: Did the customer change group-to-entitlement mappings in Okta or the Redwood SCIM/role mapper? They mentioned a groups sync earlier.
acme-platform-admin: We changed the group named `compliance-read` to `security-readonly` as part of a naming standard update. Maybe that broke the mapping.
Maria Chen: That explains it — our entitlement rule expects `compliance-read` to grant `audit_logs:read` and `retention:compliance:180d`. With the rename, no mapping fired.
Ajay Patel: Short term workaround: I can manually grant `audit_logs:read` to emma@acme.co via the Admin Console. That will restore access immediately. Would you like me to grant it for the affected users while you update Okta?
acme-platform-admin: Please do — we have an external audit starting tomorrow. Thanks.
Maria Chen: Ok doing manual grant now. Rob, can you add a small audit log to capture the manual entitlement change for compliance?
Rob Silva: Done — recorded admin action id=evt_89b1.
Kate Reynolds: Long term fix: update Okta group mapping. Steps for customer's Okta admin: 1) rename `security-readonly` back to `compliance-read` or 2) add `security-readonly` to the SCIM mapping to emit `entitlements=compliance-read` or 3) add an explicit SAML attribute `entitlements` that lists `audit_logs:read,retention:compliance:180d`. Pick one.
acme-platform-admin: We'll add `security-readonly` to the mapping (option 2). Who do we contact at Redwood if the SAML attribute grammar is wrong?
Maria Chen: Ping me and @Kate and we'll validate. Send a SAML assertion (base64) or a screenshot of attributes. I'll validate mapping rules and confirm expected entitlement names.
Ajay Patel: Note for engineering: I see entitlement-service returned empty for org_0a1b2c3d because our group->entitlement cache TTL was 15m and the group rename caused a cache miss. We should be resilient to renamed groups for a short period by falling back to SCIM identity groups. Filing a follow-up: ENG-issue 4572 to try fallback strategy.
Rob Silva: Quick repro steps we used: 1) Simulate SAML with missing `entitlements` attr, 2) request GET /api/v1/audit/logs as the subject, 3) observe 403 with body `{"error":"forbidden","message":"missing entitlement: audit_logs:read"}`. Command: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/logs`
Maria Chen: Confirmation from Acme: after Okta mapping change, access restored for emma and two other auditors. Can everyone confirm this thread is sufficient for the compliance ticket?
Kate Reynolds: I'll add a note to the compliance runbook: include group rename checklist and to verify `entitlements` attribute presence. Also included a link to ENG-issue 4572.
acme-platform-admin: TY! Will follow up if anything else pops up.
Maria Chen: Closing on our side — reach out if audit access reappears missing. :lock:
